branch_matrix.source_scope: src/arena.c:631-779,1216-1424 managed-arena small, medium and large regular-page abandonment into `pages_abandoned`, a foreign held-owner claim refusal that keeps the abandoned bit and count, retry, same-owner reassociation through `_mi_theap_page_reclaim`, foreign remote-free publication and owner collection, natural owner exit with a distinct replacement owner reclaiming on allocation, and terminal page and span release. Through the ordinary owner exit and pointer-centered free: a partly used page mapped at exit whose first foreign free unowns it again and whose last free unabandons and frees it; a full page that the generic allocation path abandons unmapped, that stays unmapped through five mostly-used foreign frees, is reabandoned to the mapped bitmap by the sixth and is unabandoned and freed by the last; and an OS-backed singleton listed in `os_abandoned_pages` until its foreign free unlinks and frees it. The `mi_abandoned_page_try_reclaim` decisions on free (own full page, foreign free with an empty or nonempty queue, foreign large page) under seven option profiles, including cross-thread reclaim through `_mi_arenas_page_unabandon` and `_mi_theap_page_reclaim`. Abandoned-page search on allocation across three arenas and two non-main heaps: each heap's own `arena_pages` record and `abandoned_count` (the main heap skips at a zero count, and a heap's drain leaves the other heap's page in the same arena), the `mi_forall_suitable_arenas` order whose `mi_arena_start_idx` start follows the heap sequence and the live heap count as sibling heaps are created and deleted, and a full drain in that order until a fresh page is needed. Concurrent interleavings, each driven deterministically by revoking access to one OS page so a source access faults and its thread waits until another thread has acted: a last foreign free that lands after the exiting owner's collection and before `mi_abandoned_page_unown`'s first head load, or between that load and its release CAS, is collected by the owner, which takes the all-free unabandon-and-free arm (src/arena.c:631-653, 1384-1409, 1286-1302); with one block still live the failed CAS's retry releases ownership and leaves the page mapped until its last free; and a free-triggered unabandon whose `mi_bitmap_clear_once_set` CAS finds the bit taken by a concurrent abandoned-page reader counts one `pages_unabandon_busy_wait` and clears it only after the reader's failed claim restores it (src/bitmap.c:109-129, 1340-1370, src/arena.c:655-671), both from the try-free caller (src/free.c:368-378) and, under `page_reclaim_on_free=1`, from the cross-thread reclaim-on-free caller (src/free.c:428-476), whose freer then owns the reclaimed page.
missing_conditions: The same unown retry after an abandonment of a full unmapped arena page or an OS-list page (src/arena.c:1339-1354 then 631-653) has no deterministic native C/Rust evidence: between their collection and the release CAS each source step writes only the page's own metadata (and, for an OS page, the Heap's `os_abandoned_pages_lock`), so revoking one OS page cannot pause the owner after its identity publication and before the CAS. Closing it needs a pause at that exact instruction, such as a hardware watchpoint or a ptrace single-step on each binary's CAS.

remaining_conditions: Qualify the arena abandonment transitions this component does not compare natively on AArch64: the unown retry after a remote free for full unmapped and OS-list page abandonment (see the abandonment branch row).
